observation_summary: The FastDateFormat class caches instances based on a key that does not correctly account for changes in the default Locale. When the default Locale is changed, subsequent calls to getDateInstance() or getDateTimeInstance() return cached instances created with the previous default Locale, leading to incorrect locale-specific formatting.
hypothesis: The caching mechanism for FastDateFormat instances uses a key that fails to incorporate the current default Locale when no explicit locale is provided. Consequently, when the default Locale changes, the cache returns stale instances associated with the old default Locale instead of creating new ones for the updated default.
prediction: The code responsible for generating the cache key in FastDateFormat will be missing the current default Locale in its construction logic, or it will be using a static reference to the default Locale that is not updated when the system default changes.
experiment_rationale: The bug report explicitly states that the HashMap key is created without the locale when it is null, and the cached object is created using the default locale at that time. The failure in the test case confirms that the cached instance is not invalidated or updated when the system default locale changes.
reasoning_summary: This is an Algorithm/Method defect because the caching logic (the procedure for retrieving/creating instances) is flawed. It fails to correctly handle the dynamic nature of the default Locale, which is a procedural error in how the cache key is computed and managed. It is not a simple missing check (Checking) or a wrong constant (Assignment/Initialization), but a flaw in the algorithmic strategy for instance retrieval.

alternative_types.why_not_primary: While a check might be added to invalidate the cache, the root cause is the design of the caching algorithm itself, which fails to account for the dependency on the mutable default Locale.
